transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brought you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you. Well, I came in because... I guess I've just been really hung up on how I look lately. I work in production, and since I started helping out with the safety trainings, I can’t seem to stop noticing my hands. When I’m pointing things out, they just look so wrinkly and uneven to me. 

And then... well, I also start looking at the photos in the company newsletter, and I keep thinking my face looks crooked in them. Other people tell me they don’t see it at all, but I just can't stop focusing on it.
On an average day, about how many hours would you say you spend thinking about or checking your hands or the way your face looks?

Well, it's not all day, but it definitely takes up some time. I'd say maybe an hour or two total, spread out. Like, before I have to do one of those safety trainings, or even before I go to my workshop at the senior center, I'll go to the bathroom and check the mirror a few times. 

I make sure to put lotion on my hands, hoping it helps the wrinkles, and I'll turn my face different ways in the light to see if it looks as crooked as I think it does. Sometimes I even ask a coworker if I look all right. It ends up making me run a little behind schedule, but... I still get myself there. It's just something I feel like I have to do before I can go out in front of people.
When your coworkers tell you they don't see any problem with your hands or face, how convinced are you, deep down, that they might be right and you might be misjudging your appearance?

Well... I guess I'm not really convinced when they say that. I mean, I hear them, and I know they're probably trying to be nice, but deep down... I just don't believe it. I look in the mirror or at those photos, and it's just so obvious to me. So even if they say I look fine, I still feel like they're either just being polite or maybe they just aren't looking as closely as I am. I still think I look the way I see myself.

Besides these concerns about your hands and face, have you noticed any other unusual thoughts, beliefs, or experiences lately—like feeling that people are watching you, talking about you, or hearing things others don't?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't hear things, and I don't feel like people are watching me or talking behind my back. It's really just... well, just me being bothered by my own hands and face. That's really the only thing going on.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient demonstrates persistent preoccupation with perceived defects in appearance (wrinkled hands, crooked face) that are not observable or appear only slight to others. This preoccupation is accompanied by repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, applying lotion, camouflaging, reassurance-seeking) consuming 1-2 hours daily and causing functional delays. Critically, the patient displays absent insight/delusional beliefs about the perceived defects—despite consistent reassurance from others, they remain firmly convinced their perception is accurate ('I still think I look the way I see myself'), meeting criteria for BDD with absent insight/delusional beliefs specifier. No other psychotic symptoms (hallucinations, persecutory delusions) are present, which argues against a primary psychotic disorder (F22) or schizophrenia, supporting BDD as the primary diagnosis rather than delusional disorder somatic type.
